journey:christ-the-king-swiebodzin.a: Mirosław Kazimierz Patecki (sculptor); initiated by Fr. Sylwester Zawadzki

x.summary: Rising above the fields outside the small town of Świebodzin in western Poland, this crowned Christ with outstretched arms was for some years the tallest statue of Jesus in the world. It stands on a raised mound, wearing a golden crown as Christ the King. The monument was the vision of a local parish priest, Fr. Sylwester Zawadzki, and was built mainly with donations from parishioners, Poles abroad and local businesses.
facts: The figure itself is 33 metres tall, one metre for each traditional year of Christ's earthly life, topped by a gilded crown 2–3 metres high (sources differ), on a mound about 16.5 metres high.
It was completed on 6 November 2010 and consecrated on 21 November 2010, the Solemnity of Christ the King, by Bishop Stefan Regmunt.
In 2018 it was reported that internet antennas had been mounted in the crown, sparking a public debate before they were removed.
